title: FOXO3 as a potential diagnostic biomarker for autophagy in rheumatoid arthritis: A bioinformatics study.
authors: Deng, Qian; Peng, Zining; Meng, Fanyu; Zeng, Wangxin; Zhu, Mengyuan; Liu, Nian; Yan, Weitian; Peng, Jiangyun
one_liner_zh: 该文通过生物信息学分析筛选类风湿关节炎自噬相关基因FOXO3作为诊断标志物，仅涉及基因表达差异与机器学习分类，无蛋白质-DNA互作体系、结合建模或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: This study aimed to identify genes associated with autophagy and potential diagnostic biomarkers by comparing the gene expression profiles of synovial tissues in patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA) and healthy individuals, aiming to offer new insights for clinical treatment strategies. We used publicly available datasets to analyze differentially expressed genes (DEGs) between the synovial tissue of RA patients and healthy individuals. Then, we intersected these DEGs with autophagy-related genes to identify autophagy genes in the synovial tissue of RA patients. We further analyzed the biological processes and functions of these genes. Furthermore, we used machine learning to identify characteristic autophagy genes in RA synovial tissue. Finally, we examined the differential expression of these characteristic genes in the blood of RA patients using an external dataset. Our study identified FOXO3 as a potential biomarker for diagnosing RA. FOXO3 gene expression was downregulated in both the synovial tissue and blood of RA patients, suggesting its involvement in multiple biological processes such as local inflammation, oxidative stress, metabolic processes, and immune responses. Our findings suggest that FOXO3 may be a novel biomarker for the clinical diagnosis of RA and may play a crucial role in the pathogenesis of RA. The study provides new insights into the molecular mechanisms of RA and potential new therapeutic targets.
abstract_zh: 本研究旨在通过比较类风湿关节炎（RA）患者与健康个体滑膜组织的基因表达谱，识别与自噬相关的基因及潜在的诊断生物标志物，以期为临床治疗策略提供新见解。我们利用公开可用的数据集，分析了RA患者与健康个体滑膜组织之间的差异表达基因（DEGs）。随后，将这些DEGs与自噬相关基因进行交集分析，以识别RA患者滑膜组织中的自噬基因。我们进一步分析了这些基因的生物学过程和功能。此外，我们采用机器学习方法识别RA滑膜组织中的特征性自噬基因。最后，我们利用外部数据集检查了这些特征基因在RA患者血液中的差异表达。我们的研究确定FOXO3为诊断RA的潜在生物标志物。FOXO3基因在RA患者的滑膜组织和血液中均表达下调，提示其参与局部炎症、氧化应激、代谢过程及免疫反应等多种生物学过程。我们的发现表明，FOXO3可能成为RA临床诊断的新型生物标志物，并在RA发病机制中发挥关键作用。本研究为RA的分子机制提供了新见解，并指出了潜在的新治疗靶点。
